importance_ranking.reason: Precast concrete houses span a wide visual range — single-room labour quarters, multi-room residential units, G+1 structures, and site offices are all visually distinct product types. Buyers use the image to confirm product type and scale before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip for a high-commitment purchase.

Floor area, configuration (BHK), structure material, and house type are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria — a contractor tendering for PMAY single-room units cannot evaluate a 3BHK villa listing. Specs are the primary shortlisting gate after visual type confirmation.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant nationally recognised brand exists in Indian precast concrete housing; the market is fragmented across regional manufacturers and buyers search by spec, capacity, and geographic reach rather than brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: This is a large-value, site-delivered, assembled structure requiring installation capability and geographic reach — government and industrial buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials, prior project track record, and service network during vendor selection. Company identity is a trust gate before price is considered.

Every sale is project-quoted — final price depends on floor area, configuration, site location, foundation scope, and installation terms. Indian buyers are price-sensitive but listed price is only a budget feasibility check after spec and company qualification; no meaningful per-unit price comparison is possible across listings.

importance_ranking.canonical_unit: per unit (per room or per house)
importance_ranking.unit_note: Larger projects may be quoted per sq ft of built-up area, but for listing display purposes the unit is always per structure unit. No buyer questions whether a prefabricated house is sold per piece.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied by the product — a finished structure is always sold per unit. No buyer confusion is possible, and project-based pricing means there is no per-unit price to qualify with a unit label.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Floor area is the single largest price driver — a 300 sq ft labour quarter vs a 1500 sq ft residential unit represents a 5–8x price difference, and values are non-interchangeable across buyer project requirements.

RCC precast, mild steel, and light gauge steel are entirely different construction systems with different structural properties, regulatory compliance paths, and price points — non-interchangeable across buyer specifications.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Government and institutional buyers specify minimum concrete grade (M30/M35/M40/M50) in tender documents per IS 456 and IS 15916; sellers need to confirm compliance and it drives structural quality differentiation.

Whether foundation work is included or excluded from the seller's scope significantly affects total project cost and a seller's ability to quote accurately; buyers frequently misunderstand what is included.

top_rfq_specs.reason: BHK configuration is non-interchangeable — sellers immediately know whether they can supply the required layout and at what price tier, making it the primary RFQ routing signal.
Floor area is the primary price driver for project-quoted structures; sellers need this to assess feasibility and provide an accurate budget estimate.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Intended use (residential vs labour camp vs site office vs farm house) defines the product type and structural/aesthetic requirements — sellers need this to confirm product suitability before configuration and area are even relevant.
Single storey vs G+1 vs G+2 significantly affects structural complexity, material quantity, and price — sellers need this to assess feasibility and quote accurately.
